frozen_original.title: RFK Jr Dismantles CDC Vaccine Advisory Committee ACIP, Fires NIH Scientists
frozen_original.synopsis: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. dissolved the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the CDC's independent expert panel that has guided vaccine policy for decades, and replaced its members with anti-vaccine advocates and skeptics. Kennedy simultaneously oversaw the firing or forced departure of hundreds of NIH scientists, many of them leaders in infectious disease and vaccine research. Public health experts warned the actions would erode vaccine confidence and leave the country unprepared for future pandemics. Former ACIP members noted their recommendations had saved millions of lives through childhood vaccination programs. Pharmaceutical industry analysts warned the changes would deter investment in vaccine development.

children.description_long: On June 9, 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). Reuters reported that Kennedy was in the process of replacing them and that many vaccine scientists protested the decision. The committee advises the CDC on how vaccines are used and by whom. Reuters also reported that the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a majority of the committee until 2028. Kennedy described the change as part of restoring public trust; experts quoted by Reuters said the dismissal could undermine confidence in health agencies. That is an attributed warning, not evidence that public confidence or vaccine access measurably changed. The CDC said the panel’s next meeting would take place June 25–27 in Atlanta. This record covers the June committee-removal action only. The source describes members being replaced, not ACIP being dissolved, and the supplied broad label for replacement members is not repeated.

children.title: HHS Layoffs Begin at NIH During a Planned 1,200-Position Reduction
children.description_short: HHS layoffs began at NIH on April 1, 2025; the department's plan targeted about 1,200 NIH positions.
children.description_medium: HHS began broad health-agency layoffs on April 1, 2025, and Reuters reported that the National Institutes of Health was among the affected agencies, with NIH employees notified of layoffs that morning. HHS’s restructuring fact sheet separately said the plan would reduce NIH’s workforce by approximately 1,200 through centralized support functions. The plan figure is a target, not proof that exactly 1,200 people were dismissed.
children.description_long: On April 1, 2025, the Trump administration began mass layoffs across federal health agencies. Reuters reported that the cuts affected the National Institutes of Health and that NIH employees had been notified early that morning that they were laid off. HHS’s restructuring fact sheet described a planned NIH workforce reduction of approximately 1,200 employees through the centralization of procurement, human resources, and communications across its 27 institutes and centers. The figure is the department’s plan, not a verified count of completed dismissals. Reuters described a broader 10,000-person reduction across health agencies, not 10,000 NIH layoffs. The supplied February 20 entry merged this workforce action with the separate June removal of ACIP members; this child isolates the NIH-related layoffs and uses the April 1 date. The source material does not establish that hundreds of the affected NIH workers were scientists, identify the number of researchers who lost jobs, or measure any resulting research interruption. It also does not show that all planned NIH reductions occurred. The record therefore describes the confirmed start of layoffs and the department’s stated target separately, without converting the target into an outcome.

children.description_long: On June 9, 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. removed all 17 members of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP). Reuters reported that Kennedy was in the process of replacing them and that many vaccine scientists protested the decision. The committee advises the CDC on how vaccines are used and by whom. Reuters also reported that the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a majority of the committee until 2028. Kennedy described the change as part of restoring public trust; experts quoted by Reuters said the dismissal could undermine confidence in health agencies. That is an attributed warning, not evidence that public confidence or vaccine access measurably changed. The CDC said the panel’s next meeting would take place June 25–27 in Atlanta. This record covers the June committee-removal action only. The source describes members being replaced, not ACIP being dissolved, and the supplied broad label for replacement members is not repeated. HHS’s release also describes ACIP as making recommendations on vaccine safety, efficacy, and clinical need to CDC.

primary.description_long:
On June 9, 2025, HHS announced that Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. had removed all 17 sitting members of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the CDC advisory committee that makes recommendations about vaccine safety, efficacy, and clinical need. HHS said new members were under consideration and framed the decision as an effort to restore public trust in vaccines.

Reuters reported that the entire 17-member panel was being replaced and that many vaccine scientists protested the move. HHS said the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and argued that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a committee majority until 2028. These are the agency’s stated rationale and reported reaction. The sources establish the committee’s removal, but they do not show what recommendations followed or measure any resulting change in vaccine uptake, safety, or health outcomes. This entry records the personnel and advisory-structure change without treating the agency’s rationale or critics’ concerns as a proven public-health consequence.

corrected_proposal.description_long:
On June 9, 2025, HHS announced that Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. had removed all 17 sitting members of the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the CDC advisory committee that makes recommendations about vaccine safety, efficacy, and clinical need. HHS said new members were under consideration and framed the decision as an effort to restore public trust in vaccines.

Reuters reported that the entire 17-member panel was being replaced and that many vaccine scientists protested the move. HHS said the members had been appointed during the Biden administration, including 13 in 2024, and argued that without their removal the Trump administration would not have been able to choose a committee majority until 2028. These are the agency’s stated rationale and reported reaction. The sources establish the committee’s removal, but they do not show what recommendations followed or measure any resulting change in vaccine uptake, safety, or health outcomes.
